description: Lebanese Red Lentil Soup, known as Adas, is a comforting and nutritious staple in Middle Eastern cuisine. This vibrant, hearty soup is made with simple ingredients like red lentils, vegetables, and aromatic spices, simmering together to create a deeply satisfying meal. It's a wholesome dish perfect for a cozy evening or as a nourishing starter, offering a taste of authentic Lebanese home cooking.

instructions.title: Prepare Vegetables
instructions.text: In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat olive oil over medium heat. Add the finely chopped onion, diced carrots, and diced celery. Sauté for 8-10 minutes until the vegetables are softened and the onion becomes translucent.

instructions.title: Add Aromatics and Spices
instructions.text: Stir in the minced garlic, ground cumin, ground coriander, and ground turmeric. Cook for another 1-2 minutes until fragrant, being careful not to burn the garlic.

instructions.title: Combine with Lentils and Broth
instructions.text: Add the rinsed red lentils, vegetable broth, and tomato paste to the pot. Stir well to combine all ingredients, ensuring the tomato paste is fully dissolved.

instructions.title: Simmer the Soup
instructions.text: Bring the soup to a boil, then reduce the heat to low. Cover the pot and let it simmer for 25-30 minutes, or until the lentils are completely tender and have broken down, thickening the soup. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking to the bottom.

instructions.title: Season and Blend
instructions.text: Season the soup with salt and black pepper to taste. For a smoother consistency, use an immersion blender to partially or fully blend the soup directly in the pot. Alternatively, carefully transfer portions to a regular blender and blend until desired smoothness is achieved, then return to the pot.

instructions.title: Final Touches and Serve
instructions.text: Stir in fresh lemon juice just before serving. Ladle the hot soup into bowls and garnish generously with fresh chopped cilantro. Serve immediately with warm pita bread or a drizzle of extra virgin olive oil.

tips: For an extra layer of flavor, toast the spices lightly in the dry pot before adding oil and vegetables.
If you prefer a thicker soup, reduce the amount of broth slightly or simmer for an additional 5-10 minutes uncovered. For a thinner soup, add more hot broth.
Leftover Adas can be stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3-4 days. It also freezes well for up to 3 months; thaw overnight in the fridge and reheat gently on the stovetop.
article:
Lebanese Red Lentil Soup, known as Adas, is more than just a dish; it's a warm embrace in a bowl, a testament to the power of simple ingredients transformed into something extraordinary. This humble yet profoundly satisfying soup holds a special place in Middle Eastern cuisine, cherished for its nourishing qualities, comforting flavor, and remarkable versatility. Whether you’re seeking a healthy weeknight meal, a hearty dish for a chilly evening, or a traditional soup for special occasions like Ramadan, Adas delivers. It’s a staple that embodies the essence of wholesome, home-cooked food, packed with plant-based protein, fiber, and vibrant flavors. This article will guide you through everything you need to know to master this delightful Middle Eastern classic, from its origins to pro tips for the perfect bowl.

## What is Lebanese Red Lentil Soup Adas?

Lebanese Red Lentil Soup, or Adas, is a beloved vegan and gluten-free soup that showcases the best of Mediterranean cooking. At its core, Adas is a thick, creamy, and flavorful soup made primarily from red lentils, aromatic vegetables, and a generous squeeze of fresh lemon juice. Unlike some other lentil soups that might incorporate meat or heavy creams, the traditional Lebanese version is often kept light and bright, relying on the natural richness of the lentils and the zing of citrus to create its distinctive profile. It’s a dish that embodies both simplicity and depth, a culinary cornerstone in Lebanon, often served as a main course with pita bread or as a comforting starter. Its popularity stems from its accessibility, nutritional value, and the deep satisfaction it provides, making it a go-to dish for families across the region.

## Ingredients You Need for Adas

The beauty of Lebanese Red Lentil Soup lies in its straightforward ingredient list. High-quality, fresh components will elevate your soup from good to truly exceptional.

Here’s what you’ll need:

*   **Red Lentils:** The star of the show. Ensure they are fresh and rinsed thoroughly. Red lentils cook quickly and break down beautifully, contributing to the soup's creamy texture.
*   **Olive Oil:** A generous amount for sautéing and drizzling, adding richness and a characteristic Mediterranean flavor.
*   **Onion & Garlic:** The aromatic foundation. Finely chopped onion and minced garlic provide essential depth and fragrance.
*   **Cumin:** The signature spice for lentil soup. Ground cumin adds warmth, earthiness, and that unmistakable Middle Eastern flavor.
*   **Salt & Black Pepper:** To taste, enhancing all the other flavors.
*   **Water or Vegetable Broth:** The liquid base. Broth will add more depth of flavor, but water works perfectly fine.
*   **Fresh Lemon Juice:** Crucial for brightening the soup and cutting through the richness of the lentils. Don't skip this!
*   **Optional Garnishes:** Fresh cilantro or parsley, extra virgin olive oil, a sprinkle of paprika or Aleppo pepper, pita bread for serving.

## Step-by-Step Instructions for Lebanese Red Lentil Soup

Creating a delicious pot of Lebanese Red Lentil Soup is surprisingly simple. Follow these steps for a consistently perfect result:

1.  **Prepare the Lentils:** Start by rinsing your red lentils thoroughly under cold running water until the water runs clear. This removes any debris and excess starch. Drain well and set aside.
2.  **Sauté Aromatics:** In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat a good drizzle of olive oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and sauté for 5-7 minutes, or until softened and translucent. Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant, being careful not to burn it.
3.  **Add Lentils and Spices:** Stir in the rinsed lentils and ground cumin. Cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly, to toast the spices and coat the lentils. This step enhances the flavor of the cumin.
4.  **Add Liquid and Simmer:** Pour in the water or vegetable broth. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover the pot, and let it simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the lentils are completely tender and have started to break down. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
5.  **Blend (Optional):** For a smoother consistency, you can use an immersion blender to partially or fully blend the soup directly in the pot. If you don't have an immersion blender, carefully transfer batches to a regular blender and blend until desired smoothness, then return to the pot. I recommend leaving some texture for a more rustic feel.
6.  **Season and Finish:** Stir in the fresh lemon juice, salt, and black pepper to taste. Taste and adjust seasonings as needed. The lemon juice is key, so don't be shy!
7.  **Serve:** Ladle the hot Lebanese Red Lentil Soup into bowls. Drizzle with a little extra virgin olive oil and garnish with fresh chopped cilantro or parsley, if desired.

## Pro Tips for the Best Adas Results

Achieving the perfect bowl of Lebanese Red Lentil Soup is easy with a few expert tips:

*   **Don't Skimp on Lemon Juice:** The fresh tang of lemon juice is what truly elevates Adas. It brightens the soup and balances the earthy lentils. Add it at the very end to preserve its fresh flavor.
*   **Use Good Quality Olive Oil:** A generous drizzle of high-quality extra virgin olive oil, both in the cooking process and as a finishing touch, adds a rich, fruity depth.
*   **Taste and Adjust:** Seasoning is personal. Always taste your soup before serving and adjust salt, pepper, and lemon juice to your preference. A pinch of cayenne pepper can add a subtle kick.
*   **Achieve Desired Consistency:** If your soup is too thick, add a splash more hot water or broth until it reaches your preferred consistency. If it's too thin, let it simmer uncovered for a few more minutes.
*   **Fresh Herbs Make a Difference:** A sprinkle of fresh cilantro or parsley before serving not only adds a pop of color but also a burst of fresh flavor.

## Serving Suggestions for Your Lebanese Lentil Soup

Lebanese Red Lentil Soup is incredibly versatile and can be enjoyed in many ways. Here are some popular serving suggestions:

*   **With Pita Bread:** This is the classic pairing. Warm pita bread, torn into pieces, is perfect for dipping and scooping up the hearty soup.
*   **Crusty Bread or Croutons:** Any crusty bread, toasted bread, or homemade croutons can be a delicious accompaniment.
*   **Fresh Salad:** A light, refreshing side salad, such as a simple cucumber and tomato salad or a vibrant fattoush, provides a lovely contrast to the warm soup.
*   **Rice:** For a more substantial meal, some people enjoy a small side of plain white rice.
*   **Additional Garnishes:** Beyond olive oil and herbs, consider a sprinkle of sumac for extra tang, a pinch of red pepper flakes for heat, or even some fried minced garlic as a crunchy topping.

## Variations and Substitutions for Adas

While the classic Lebanese Red Lentil Soup is perfect as is, you can easily customize it to suit your taste or available ingredients:

*   **Add Vegetables:** Incorporate finely diced carrots, celery, or even a potato along with the onions and garlic for added nutrients and texture.
*   **Spice It Up:** For an extra layer of flavor, consider adding a pinch of turmeric for color and earthy notes, or a touch of smoked paprika for a deeper, smoky taste. A pinch of cayenne or a few chili flakes can introduce a pleasant heat.
*   **Broth Choice:** While water is traditional, using vegetable broth will undoubtedly add more depth and umami to your soup.
*   **Herb Variations:** If you're not a fan of cilantro, parsley is an excellent alternative. Mint can also offer a unique, refreshing twist.
*   **Garnish Creativity:** Experiment with a swirl of plain yogurt (if not strictly vegan), toasted nuts, or even a sprinkle of za'atar for an authentic touch.

## Storage and Reheating Tips

Lebanese Red Lentil Soup is one of those dishes that often tastes even better the next day, as the flavors have more time to meld.

*   **Refrigeration:** Store leftover Adas in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3-4 days.
*   **Freezing:** This soup freezes beautifully. Allow it to cool completely, then transfer it to freezer-safe containers or bags. It can be frozen for up to 3 months. Thaw overnight in the refrigerator before reheating.
*   **Reheating:** Reheat gently on the stovetop over medium-low heat, stirring occasionally, until warmed through. If the soup has thickened too much in the fridge, add a splash of water or vegetable broth to reach your desired consistency. You can also reheat individual portions in the microwave.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

**Q: Is Lebanese Red Lentil Soup vegan and gluten-free?**
A: Yes, traditional Adas is naturally vegan, vegetarian, and gluten-free, making it a fantastic option for a wide range of dietary preferences.

**Q: Do I need to soak the red lentils before cooking?**
A: No, red lentils cook very quickly and break down easily, so soaking is generally not necessary. Just a good rinse is sufficient.

**Q: Can I use other types of lentils?**
A: While red lentils are traditional and contribute to the creamy texture, you could use split yellow lentils. Green or brown lentils will hold their shape more and require a longer cooking time, resulting in a different texture.

**Q: How can I make my Adas thicker or thinner?**
A: To make it thicker, let it simmer uncovered for a bit longer. To thin it out, simply add more hot water or vegetable broth until you reach your desired consistency.

**Q: What is the difference between Lebanese lentil soup and other Middle Eastern lentil soups?**
A: While many Middle Eastern countries have their versions of lentil soup, Lebanese Red Lentil Soup is particularly known for its bright, lemony flavor profile and often simpler ingredient list, focusing on the lentils, aromatics, and cumin, with a significant emphasis on fresh lemon juice. Other versions might include carrots, celery, or different spice blends.

This humble bowl of Lebanese Red Lentil Soup is a testament to the fact that the most satisfying meals often come from the simplest ingredients. With its comforting warmth, vibrant flavors, and incredible health benefits, Adas is a dish that nourishes both body and soul. Give this recipe a try, and you'll quickly understand why it’s a beloved staple across the Middle East. Enjoy the process of creating this wholesome, delicious soup, and savor every spoonful!
